I think it depends on the person and the type of book. At this point in my life, I've probably purchased Cats Cradle a handful of times, and have given away each copy to friends who have never read it. I've given out first edition books in rough condition solely based on the material and the fact that the person really appreciated it more, as opposed to a recent edition. Some people like new books, and some like early editions.

Used books are more of a "it's the weekend, and you deserve a gift for no real occasion" type of gift. Or as a "here is some booze as the main gift, but this book is an added bonus"

The only thing is these days I'm the only person in my family that still reads books, everyone else just does them on audible.

You know they say; It's the thought that counts. I would give the book if it's in serviceable shape, give it along with another gift if you are truly concerned about how the other person might take the notion of receiving a used gift.

Only collectors care and the vain care about the condition. Any avid read will care more about what the book is about and picking a book that fits the reader is a really great gift regardless of the condition as long as the binding isn't falling apart.

I don't give books in association with commercialized gift times (birthdays, anniversaries, x-mas), I tried in the past and learned that people generally hate it. There are some rare exceptions, those you know intimately and know will love XYZ book without a shadow of a doubt. I wouldn't even put my wife in that category, she's constantly surprising me what what she likes and what she doesn't... guess 15 years isn't enough time to get to know those preferences.

Anyway, I just don't give books as gifts when gifts are expected. I give them when they are unexpected, out of the blue... "Happy Tuesday!". You get a chance to explain why you thought of it for them without it being half heard/remembered due to the fracas that surrounds traditional gift times. For the known book-lovers on commercial gift days, they get gift cards or handmade "Lets go book shopping, on me" promise cards.

That said, I'm a HUGE library advocate. I probably have fewer than 10 physical books that I own, in my house (all niche-market stuff, things I can't get from a library ~ yes, those items do exist). Everyone knows this and I encourage them to use/support/donate to the library. So not a whole lot of books moving around as possessions in my immediate family.

I wouldn't give a used book if new were available though, unless there were something unique about it. Advanced reader copy, author/illustrator signed, out of print cover, etc...

It sort of depends on your circumstances and that of the person to whom you are giving. I would give new if I could afford it, but used if that's all I could manage and if I knew that the recipient would love reading my heartfelt selection. And if I was giving to someone with little money for books, I would give a few used books that I loved reading to give them more enjoyment. People who can't afford to buy their own books and who love to read would probably not be picky about the new vs used, they would probably appreciate the added enjoyment of multiple books.

Of course, rare books would be in their own category. My husband collects vinyl albums, and would love a collectible rare album that would only be available as used.
Yes. Some books are only available as used and can be an excellent gift.
